# CLAUDE.md — "Heard"

Conventions and guardrails for building this app. **Read `SPEC.md` for the full spec and `BUILD_PLAN.md` for the milestone order.** This file holds the rules you must follow on every change.

## What this is
A two-sided marketplace where customers pay to talk with companion listeners who are all legally blind or visually impaired. Non-clinical companionship — **never** therapy. Accessibility and the dignity of providers are the whole point of the product.

## Stack
Next.js (App Router) · TypeScript (`strict`) · Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Storage) · Tailwind CSS · Zod · Vitest + React Testing Library + Playwright · deploy to Vercel + Supabase.

## Golden rules (do not violate)
1. **Accessibility is non-negotiable.** WCAG 2.2 AA minimum, AAA contrast on body text. Keyboard-operable, visible focus, semantic HTML, labeled controls, no state by color alone. A screen isn't done until it passes axe in tests. See `SPEC.md` §10.
2. **External services only through adapters.** Reach payments/calls/background-checks via `lib/integrations/*/index.ts` (`getPayments()`, `getCalls()`, `getBackgroundCheck()`). Never import `mock.ts`/`real.ts` directly; never call Stripe/Zoom/Checkr SDKs outside `real.ts`. Default mode is `mock`.
3. **All money is integer cents.** No floats for currency. All pricing/commission math lives in `lib/pricing.ts` and nowhere else. Commission comes from `PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE` (config), never a literal.
4. **Security: RLS on every table.** Customers/providers touch only their own rows; public reads only approved-provider public fields; admin sees all. The `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is server-only — never shipped to the client, never in a client component.
5. **Validate at the boundary.** Every server action and route handler validates input with Zod and checks the caller's role/ownership before doing work.
6. **Server-first.** Prefer React Server Components + Server Actions; use client components only for genuinely interactive UI. No secrets in client bundles.
7. **All user-facing copy goes through `messages/en.json`** (i18n-ready) — no hard-coded strings in components.
8. **Safety framing in the product.** Every page carries the "companionship, not therapy — crisis support" affordance. Don't add anything that implies medical/mental-health treatment.

## Conventions
- Components: PascalCase files; one component per file; design-system primitives in `components/ui` (Button, Field, Card, Dialog, …) used everywhere for consistent a11y.
- Styling: Tailwind core utilities + the design tokens from `../Interactive_Prototype_Design_Brief.md` (warm & trustworthy palette, 18px+ body, ≥48px tap targets).
- Data access: queries in `lib/db/queries.ts`; Zod schemas in `lib/validation/schemas.ts`.
- Errors: never swallow; return typed results and show friendly, accessible error states.
- Tests live in `tests/`; add/extend tests with every feature.

## Commands
```
npm run dev            # local dev
npm run build          # production build
npm run lint           # eslint + prettier
npm run typecheck      # tsc --noEmit
npm run test           # vitest (unit + component)
npm run test:e2e       # playwright
supabase db reset      # apply migrations + seed (6 sample providers)
```

## Definition of done (every feature/PR)
- TypeScript passes (`strict`), lint clean.
- Keyboard-navigable + axe a11y check passes for any new/changed screen.
- New logic has unit tests; pricing/accounting changes have explicit cases (blocks, overage, commission, tips, rounding).
- Inputs Zod-validated; RLS/ownership respected; no secrets client-side.
- User-facing strings in `messages/en.json`.

## Out of scope right now
Real Stripe/Zoom/Checkr calls, moderation/reporting admin UI (table + minimal report hook only), native mobile, subscriptions. Keep schema/adapters ready so these don't need a rewrite. See `SPEC.md` §12.

findings.title: Link>Button polymorphism pattern creates confusing visual nesting
findings.detail: Throughout the app, links wrap Button components with className="rounded-btn" to make them appear as buttons. This pattern repeats 20+ times across app/(marketing), app/(customer), app/(provider), app/(admin), and page layouts. The Link's rounded-btn className is redundant with Button's styling, and the pattern is semantically unclear: the visual style comes from Button, but the semantic meaning comes from Link. This creates maintenance debt and reduces readability.
findings.pointer: app/(marketing)/page.tsx:1-200 (lines with <Link href=".." className="rounded-btn"><Button>), app/(customer)/account/page.tsx:100+, app/(provider)/provider/dashboard/page.tsx:50+, others
findings.recommendation: Create a LinkButton component that unifies these concerns: export const LinkButton = React.forwardRef(({ href, variant, children, ...rest }, ref) => (<Link href={href}><Button {...rest}>{children}</Button></Link>)). Replace all 20+ instances. This eliminates visual duplication and clarifies intent.

findings.title: Hardcoded commission rate (95%/5%) in user-facing copy
findings.detail: The message at messages/en.json:"provider.step3Help" contains "You keep 95% — Heard's fee is 5%." This is a magic number that violates CLAUDE.md rule 3 (commission comes from PLATFORM_COMMISSION_RATE, never a literal). If the commission rate changes, this message will be stale and contradictory to the actual rate shown on the admin dashboard (which reads getCommissionRate()). The rate should be computed dynamically at render time, not hardcoded.
findings.recommendation: Refactor provider/onboarding/page.tsx to compute and interpolate the provider's take-home percentage dynamically: const providerTakeHome = (1 - getCommissionRate()) * 100; then use t("provider.step3Help", { takeHome: providerTakeHome.toFixed(0), fee: (getCommissionRate() * 100).toFixed(1) }) with a message template.

findings.title: Unsafe type casts with 'as unknown' in PublicProvider queries
findings.detail: lib/db/queries.ts uses (data ?? []) as unknown as PublicProvider[] in 4+ places (listApprovedProviders, getApprovedProvider, getApprovedProvidersByIds, and others). The double cast 'as unknown as' bypasses TypeScript's type safety. These should either use proper type guards or rely on the Supabase client's generic type parameter if it's available. This pattern weakens type safety and could hide runtime errors.
findings.pointer: lib/db/queries.ts: lines with 'as unknown as PublicProvider[]' pattern (appears ~4 times in provider query functions)
findings.recommendation: Replace with proper type narrowing or rely on Supabase's generic query types. Alternatively, add a type guard: const isPublicProvider = (x: unknown): x is PublicProvider => typeof x === 'object' && x !== null && 'id' in x...

findings.title: Duplicate STATUS/PAY_STATUS pattern objects in different dashboards
findings.detail: app/(customer)/account/page.tsx defines PAY_STATUS as a Record mapping payment statuses to { labelKey, tone, icon }, and app/(provider)/provider/dashboard/page.tsx defines a similar STATUS Record for provider status. These follow the same pattern but aren't shared. Any future enum of statuses (e.g., for sessions) will repeat this pattern again, creating inconsistent maintenance points.
findings.recommendation: Extract a reusable type and helper: export type StatusConfig<T extends string> = Record<T, { labelKey: MessageKey; tone: StatusTone; icon?: LucideIcon }>. Move common status maps to lib/constants.ts or a new lib/dashboard-patterns.ts, imported by both dashboards.

findings.title: Deliberate error swallowing in Dialog.tsx catch blocks lacks rationale comment
findings.detail: components/ui/Dialog.tsx contains two catch blocks (lines ~30, ~36) that silently fall back to using dialog.open = true instead of dialog.showModal(). This is intentional (for jsdom support in tests), but the catch blocks have no body—just catch { ... fallback }. While the outer comment explains the pattern, the individual catch blocks could be clearer about why they swallow the error.
findings.recommendation: Add a comment in each catch block: } catch { /* showModal not available (e.g., in jsdom); safe to ignore */ dialog.open = true; }

findings.title: VoiceIntroRecorder error handling uses generic message for multiple failure modes
findings.detail: components/provider/VoiceIntroRecorder.tsx catches all errors (both during recording and upload) and sets the same error message t("provider.recordingUnsupported"). This conflates permission denials, unsupported browser features, and upload failures. Users get the same message whether they denied microphone access, the browser doesn't support recording, or the upload failed—making it harder to debug.
findings.recommendation: Differentiate error types: catch DOMException with code 'NotAllowedError' → 'Microphone was denied'; other exceptions → 'Browser doesn't support recording'; network/upload errors → 'Upload failed'. Provide separate i18n keys.

findings.title: Inconsistent table column naming across dashboards
findings.detail: The provider SessionsTable uses "minutesShort" helper for block/overage display, while the customer PastSessionsTable shows durationLabel (already formatted). Provider PayoutsTable uses different column names (periodLabel, amountCents) than admin ActivityTables (colPeriod, colAmount). This inconsistency makes it harder to extend or unify table logic later.
findings.pointer: components/provider/SessionsTable.tsx (block/overageMinutes rendering), components/customer/PastSessionsTable.tsx (durationLabel), components/admin/AdminActivityTables.tsx (different naming conventions)
findings.recommendation: Standardize table column data shapes: create a shared interface or utility that normalizes how tables receive date, amount, duration, and status columns. Use consistent naming (e.g., always 'amountCents' not 'amount_cents', always 'periodStartMs' for sortable dates).

findings.title: No test coverage for earnings aggregation edge cases
findings.detail: lib/earnings.ts computes week/month/lifetime earnings aggregations with hardcoded WEEK_MS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000 and date math for month boundaries (startOfMonthMs). There are no unit tests for edge cases like: sessions/tips spanning month/week boundaries, invalid/missing ISO dates in the rows, or daylight-saving-time edge cases. The earnings breakdown is shown in dashboards and could be incorrect if aggregation logic breaks.
findings.pointer: lib/earnings.ts (no corresponding test file found; no entries in tests/unit/earnings.test.ts for these functions)
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests in tests/unit/earnings.test.ts for: earnings spanning week/month boundaries, missing/null created_at/ended_at, sessions in different years, DST transitions. Use injected nowMs for deterministic dates.

findings.title: Provider data access uses RLS but doesn't document RLS policy expectations
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md rule 4 mandates "RLS on every table" and the code uses Supabase RLS, but there's no schema documentation or comments explaining which queries rely on RLS and which need explicit WHERE clauses. For example, listCustomerBookings should use RLS to filter by customer_id, but there's no comment confirming RLS is active. If RLS is accidentally disabled or the policy is wrong, the breach won't be obvious from the code.
findings.recommendation: Add a comment block at the top of db/queries.ts documenting which tables have RLS and which queries depend on it. Example: "// bookings table has RLS: authenticated users can read/write only their own rows (customer_id or provider_id). Admin queries use service role and bypass RLS."

findings.title: Orphaned or unused i18n keys (potential dead code)
findings.detail: messages/en.json contains keys like 'page.browseTitle', 'page.browseComingSoon', 'page.accountTitle', etc. (under the 'page' namespace) that appear to be deprecated or unused. A systematic grep for all keys in .tsx/.ts files should be done to identify orphaned keys that can be removed and reduce maintenance burden.
findings.recommendation: Run: grep -ro 't("[^"]*"' app components lib | cut -d'"' -f2 | sort -u > used.txt, then identify keys in messages/en.json not in used.txt. Remove unused keys and document the removal in the next build.

findings.title: Magic number in maxMinutes for call session creation
findings.detail: app/(customer)/session/actions.ts line ~53 creates a call session with maxMinutes: booking.block_minutes + 15 (a hardcoded +15 minute buffer). This magic number isn't documented or configurable. If the policy changes, the code won't be obvious to the next person.
findings.recommendation: Extract to a constant: const CALL_SESSION_BUFFER_MINUTES = 15; and add a comment explaining why (e.g., "Buffer to allow overage time beyond the block").

findings.title: Nested form state function in auth actions could be shared
findings.detail: app/(auth)/actions.ts defines fieldErrorsFrom() to extract Zod validation errors into a field map. This same pattern likely appears in other action files (customer, provider, admin). Extracting Zod error results to field errors is a common pattern that should be centralized.
